newsitem.title: CUBA: For big cigar fans -- a 9-footer.
newsitem.headline: For big cigar fans -- a 9-footer.

text.p: A Cuban cigar roller is seeking a place in the record books after making a cigar that stands almost double his own height at 9.51 feet (2.90 meters) long, Cuban media said on Wednesday.
The cigar is not for smoking, but is on display at Havana's cigar museum.
Its maker, Manuel Guzman, told the ruling Communist Party daily Granma that he took a week to make it. The newspaper did not say when he completed the cigar.

Guzman, 70, rolled cigars as a youth but after Cuba's 1959 revolution became a teacher and eventually a university professor of Marxism. After retirement he went back to rolling cigars and now works in tourist hotels selling his products.
Guzman told Granma he set to work on a record cigar after reading that the Guinness Book of Records lists the world's largest cigar as being 7.70 feet (2.35 meters) long and located in Madrid.
The world's biggest cigar should be in the country that makes the world's best cigars, Granma quoted Guzman as saying.
